{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.", "text": "Mara went. She killed the lamp in the front room on her way past, and the dark rushed in so fast she had to feel her way along the hall, one hand on the wallpaper, the other clutching the ledger to her chest. Behind her, she heard Eli's sock feet thump up the stairs and June's small voice asking something he didn't answer.

The cellar door stuck the way it always did. She put her shoulder to it, and it gave with a groan that seemed loud enough to carry all the way to the road. Cool air breathed up at her, smelling of dirt and apples gone soft. She didn't dare turn on the bulb.

Seven steps down. She counted them. At the bottom she found the shelves by memory, running her fingers over the dusty lids of the peach jars until she reached the end of the row. Behind them, the wall was rough plank instead of stone. She pushed, and a board swung inward on leather hinges, just as she'd once watched Grandpa do when he thought she was asleep on the stairs.

Something was already inside. Her fingers brushed oilcloth, and beneath it, the long, hard shape of metal.

She didn't let herself think about it. She slid the ledger in beside it, eased the board shut, and set the jars back in their dust rings.

Overhead, the engine died. A car door opened and closed, gentle, almost polite.

Then came three knocks on the front door, evenly spaced, and a man's voice said, "Evening, Ruth. I believe you have something of mine.""}
